AnalysisView.description:
What the Gap page reads after a reload, a restart, or a teammate opening
the project (round 17, F-02).
AnalysisView.title: AnalysisView

ArtifactFreshnessView.description:
**One advisory per artifact, expandable to per-analysis detail.**

`manual`-class in the UI's sense and **never a refusal**: it is not inserted
into the manual-gap collection the export gate refuses on. `readiness` is the
artifact's own `source_analysis_state`, passed through — freshness and
readiness are different questions and this model keeps them apart.
ArtifactFreshnessView.title: ArtifactFreshnessView

AssertNotApplicableRequest.description:
No free-text reason, by design (round 21, F-11): an unbounded, durable,
user-controlled field with no storage or redaction contract is a liability
rather than an explanation. The audit row records who and when.
AssertNotApplicableRequest.title: AssertNotApplicableRequest

AuthoredArtifact.description: The unit that is governed, attested and handed off.
AuthoredArtifact.title: AuthoredArtifact

CarriedAnalysisView.description: One inherited analysis, as the expandable detail shows it.
CarriedAnalysisView.title: CarriedAnalysisView

CheckpointDiff.description:
What changed between two checkpoints of one run.

``truncated`` is the platform's own admission that the diff is partial, and
it is carried rather than dropped: a truncated diff presented as a whole one
is the same defect as an incomplete trace presented as complete.
CheckpointDiff.title: CheckpointDiff

CheckpointPage.description:
One page of a run's checkpoints, in sequence order.

**``complete`` and ``dropped`` are not here, and the reason is upstream**
`[0.8.0, Phase-5 own audit]`. This class carried them, with a docstring
saying they were *"carried for the same reason the trace carries them: a
strip that cannot say whether it is showing all of them invites the reader
to conclude things from an absence."* That sentence is **true of the
trace** — `TraceResponse` declares both — and was copied onto a response
that has neither: `CheckpointListResponse` declares nine fields and neither
of these is among them. `kneo_client`'s own mapper says so in as many words,
and reads them with `getattr(..., None)` precisely because they *"exist only
on the trace response"*.

So both were structurally **always ``null``**, the SPA's
``complete === false`` branch could never fire, and this docstring promised
a reader something the platform does not send. Publishing a branch nothing
can fill is `A3`'s defect in the other direction — there the contract
declared responses no handler could produce; here it declared fields no
upstream could populate.

**When `kneo_serv` adds them to the checkpoint list**, restore both fields
here, restore the strip's warning, and say so — the projection already reads
them through the same `Page`, so it is a schema change and a UI branch, not
a new call.
CheckpointPage.title: CheckpointPage

ComponentFreshnessView.description: One contributing component, at the bytes S4 froze it at.
ComponentFreshnessView.title: ComponentFreshnessView

CreateProjectRequest.description:
What a client may say when creating a project: a name, and nothing else.

**No path field, deliberately.** The server allocates
`<workspace_base>/<project-id>`, so an ordinary principal has no input that
reaches the filesystem — which is what makes managed creation safe for them
while *attaching* an existing tree stays an operator-only host command
(`bff_routers`, ADR-009). A `root` field here would be the whole difference.
CreateProjectRequest.title: CreateProjectRequest

DraftReassociationView.description: What the new ref now carries.
DraftReassociationView.title: DraftReassociationView

DraftRef.description:
Identity **is** the canonical project-relative path (round 3, F-10).

The file-first model makes git and external renames normal events, and a
store id would need reconciliation semantics for both. ``revision`` is the
SHA-256 of current bytes, so a write has a precondition to check.
DraftRef.title: DraftRef

DraftRefBody.description: The draft being asserted about, by path and expected revision.
DraftRefBody.title: DraftRefBody

Environment.description:
The project-scoped **alias** and URL only.

Never ``profile_name`` — that is server-side configuration — and never the
key. An earlier shape exposed ``name``, which would have leaked the profile
identifier and generated a SPA type unable to send the documented alias
(round 2, F-14).
Environment.title: Environment

ErrorEnvelope.description:
The body **every** refusal carries, as a published schema `[0.8.0 A3]`.

`api_contract.md` has specified this shape since 0.1.0 and the BFF has
returned it since the Phase-5 audit universalised it. What was never true is
the **published** contract: FastAPI inferred `HTTPValidationError` —
`{"detail": [...]}` — onto 55 of 60 operations, a body no handler here can
produce, and published none of this one.

That is not a new discovery. `create_app`'s own comment records it as the
reason `/docs` was switched off: *"what it published was not true … an
interactive console that answers 'what does this API do' with a wrong answer
is worse than no console, because it is believed."* Turning off the **viewer**
left the **artifact** — which is what the SPA's types are generated from under
ADR-011, and the only thing a client author reads — saying the same wrong
thing, and `gen_openapi.py --check` stayed green because the committed file
faithfully reproduced the inference.

It is the body of **every refusal status an operation declares** — each
`422`, each scaffold `501`, and each status a route lists in `responses=` —
attached by one publisher rather than by each route, so a route declaring a
refusal gets this body without naming it. The one declared non-2xx that is not
an envelope is `GET /api/readyz`'s `503`, a readiness probe's answer, which
publishes its own `Readiness` body.

**A declared status is a floor, not the enumeration.** An operation can refuse
with a status it does not declare (most do not list `401`, `403`, `404` or
`409`); the codes a client can switch on are enumerated in `api_contract.md`'s
refusal vocabulary, and every one answered in a response body arrives in this
shape (the OIDC callback's codes travel in a redirect's query string instead).

code.description: A stable, switchable refusal code. Never prose.
code.title: Code

details.description: Per-refusal structure, present when the refusal has one. `request_invalid` carries `errors`, pydantic's per-field list with the offending `input` removed; a route's own refusal may carry nothing here.
details.title: Details

message.description: A human sentence. Never switched on by a client.
examples: The request body did not match the endpoint's schema.
message.title: Message

request_id.description: Always present, so every failure is traceable end to end. Carries the upstream platform id when the platform produced the failure.
request_id.title: Request Id

ErrorEnvelope.title: ErrorEnvelope

ExportView.description:
What `GET …/artifacts/{id}/export` returns.

The route returned a bare `dict`, so the OpenAPI described it as
`additionalProperties: true` with no shape and the SPA's generated types
could say nothing about it — the hand-off page fell back to
`Record<string, unknown>` and rendered the whole envelope as JSON rather
than the spec (Phase-5 audit, B6). A typed response is what makes the
ADR-011 generation chain reach this route at all.
ExportView.title: ExportView

ExposureView.description: What an owner must read before registering, and confirm afterwards.
ExposureView.title: ExposureView

FreshnessOffer.description:
An operation the user may run — **never a claim about what it will do**.

The store decides the effect and the projection is re-read afterwards. There
is no "this import will supersede" and no "re-importing cannot help": four
review rounds each produced a version of that sentence and execution refuted
each one.
FreshnessOffer.title: FreshnessOffer

GapRef.description: A gap's identity. Never a bare ``gap_id`` (round 20, F-01).
GapRef.title: GapRef

GapResolutionRequest.description:
One adjudication, bound to one card and one exact revision.

**No free-text note, and its absence is a decision** (r3 F-03). The first draft
required one, unbounded and durable — which is exactly the field
`gap_acknowledgement.note` was removed for: user-controlled content with no size,
redaction, encryption or retention contract. Who attested, when, which card and
against which bytes *is* the record.
GapResolutionRequest.title: GapResolutionRequest

GapResolutionView.description:
The effective state after the call, recomputed from the log.

`outstanding_blocking_gaps` is **recomputed server-side at that revision** rather
than being derived by the client from a stale local list, so one round trip tells
an author exactly what remains. `GapRef` pairs, never bare ids — a bare `gap_id`
is unique only within one analysis (r4 F-03).
GapResolutionView.title: GapResolutionView

GovernRequest.description: No alias, no draft, no overlays — the artifact carries all of it.
GovernRequest.title: GovernRequest

GraphEdge.description:
One transition.

``label`` and ``conditional`` are **independent**: upstream compiles a
condition to a callable it cannot serialize, so it sends only the boolean
``conditional`` alongside a free ``label``. An earlier version of this model
invented a single ``condition`` string from them, which would have drawn a
gated edge as a plain one whenever the label was absent.

``priority`` is not projected: it exists upstream but is always ``0`` for
spec-compiled graphs, so rendering it would imply an ordering that is not
there.
GraphEdge.title: GraphEdge

GraphNode.description:
One node of the compiled topology.

``label`` projects the platform's ``name``; a ``sequential`` step's ``kind``
is ``null`` upstream and becomes ``"step"`` here so the canvas always has
something to render. The node error-policy fields the platform also sends
(``on_error``, ``fallback_node``, ``max_retries``, ``timeout_seconds``) are
deliberately not projected yet — they are `graph`-family only and belong
with the editor read path, not the topology spike.
GraphNode.title: GraphNode

GraphView.description:
The **platform-rendered** topology (ADR-004).

Studio never derives a graph from the YAML, so the picture and the spec
cannot disagree. ``available`` is false when the workflow family has no
topology to draw — the SPA must render that state rather than an empty
canvas that looks like a broken one.

``sequential`` **does** render: upstream serializes it as a linear chain.
Only orchestration, handoff, group-chat and agent-only specs return
``workflow_kind: null``, and upstream does not say *which*, so the reason
string here is necessarily general until the effective spec is built (0.2.0)
and its own ``workflow.type`` can name the family.
GraphView.title: GraphView

ImportResult.description:
**Import is draft-only in 0.1.0, in both binding states.**

``artifact`` and ``portability`` are ``null`` unconditionally. The bound
branch requires and validates an alias and then writes a draft like any
other; creating the artifact is the separate, explicit
``POST …/artifacts`` step.

The fields stay on the model rather than being removed: the shape is the
0.2.0 target, and a client that already reads them keeps working when they
start being populated. What was wrong was the *documentation* — three
published pages and the SPA all described a bound import returning an
artifact, so the SPA carried a branch that could never run
(external review, F-10).
ImportResult.title: ImportResult

LineageFreshnessView.description:
One lineage — the four-member key — beneath a component.

Two sources with identical output are two lineages, each with its own outcome
and its own offers; a version that counted live matches without grouping this
way read them as one unorderable lineage.
LineageFreshnessView.title: LineageFreshnessView

ManifestEntry.description:
One registered ref, annotated with why it counts or does not.

`privileged` is the annotation that matters: those are the entries that
feed `exposure_digest`, so they are what an owner is being asked about.
Studio-created drafts are listed too — an owner deciding what sharing this
tree reveals should see the whole manifest, not the subset that happens to
move the digest.
ManifestEntry.title: ManifestEntry

PlatformTestRun.description:
The **platform's** view of a started run — its lifecycle, not Studio's.

Present only when `StudioTestRun.status` is ``started``, and read live from
``platform.runs.get`` against the run's *recorded* binding. ``status`` here may
independently be queued, running, blocked, completed or failed while Studio's own
status stays ``started``: Studio records that it knows one platform id, and does
not mirror the platform lifecycle into its row.
PlatformTestRun.title: PlatformTestRun

Portability.description: ``handoffable ⇔ blockers == []``. Recomputed per read, never persisted.
Portability.title: Portability

PreflightCredentialsView.description:
The credential references the platform exposes for this artifact's frozen
binding — **redacted entries, never values**.

``credentials`` is keyed by section (``providers``, ``extra``,
``service_tokens``), each mapping a name to the platform's redacted entry
(``present``/``status``/``env_var``…). ``None`` when ``state`` is ``unavailable``.
PreflightCredentialsView.title: PreflightCredentialsView

PreflightPolicyView.description:
The target environment's policy, as the platform holds it for this artifact's
frozen binding.

``policy`` is the platform's own body, untyped on the wire (`kneo_serv` returns a
free-form policy object), passed through rather than re-modelled so Studio cannot
quietly drop a key the Dashboard shows. ``None`` when ``state`` is ``unavailable``,
or when the platform holds no policy for the environment.
PreflightPolicyView.title: PreflightPolicyView

PreviewRequest.description:
The editor's buffer, and which draft it is a buffer *for*.

**`alias` is required, and round 2's F-02 is why.** Preview calls the platform, and
`client_for(runtime, project_id, alias, …)` cannot be built without one — the
artifact-addressed govern routes take theirs from the artifact row, and preview has
no artifact. Omitting it made the first version of this contract unimplementable
rather than merely thin.
PreviewRequest.title: PreviewRequest

PreviewView.description:
`{revision, ok, stages}` — one entry per stage that RAN, in order.

**A stage that did not run is absent**, which is how *validate-not-run* and
*compile-not-run* are distinguished without inventing a third truth value. Compile
is absent exactly when validate failed, because that is what
`validate_then_compile` actually does.

`ok` is true only if every stage ran **and** every stage passed.

`revision` is the request's own, copied verbatim: advisory as an input — preview
judges the text, not the file — and echoed so a client can discard a response that
raced its own buffer. Round 3's F-02 found four paragraphs promising that echo
while the model had no field to carry it.
PreviewView.title: PreviewView

ProjectLimits.description:
Read-only, and no principal changes a cap (round 22, F-09). In this cut
the caps are fixed module constants — no command raises one yet (r12 F-03).
ProjectLimits.title: ProjectLimits

Readiness.description:
What a probe is told. Short on purpose.

No version, no configuration, no counts: this answers unauthenticated, so
everything in it is public, and an availability probe is not a place to
publish facts about a deployment.
Readiness.title: Readiness

ReassociationRequest.description: Both refs, the revision they must **both** hold, and the exposure aggregate.
ReassociationRequest.title: ReassociationRequest

RegisterRequest.description:
Registering a file that already existed under the project root.

``exposure_digest`` is a **compare-and-set**, not an audit field: it proves
the caller read the project's current exposure before widening it. Without
it an owner adds entries one at a time, each individually reasonable, and
never faces the aggregate — which is how the manifest gets rebuilt into the
exposure it exists to prevent (round 22, F-06).
RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest

RelatedRef.description:
A draft this analysis relates to, and what that file holds **right now**.

**The Gap page's identity problem, solved server-side** (0.3.0, r3 F-01). The page
receives only an `analysisId` and its routes carry no draft ref, so it cannot
construct a resolution request — which needs both a `ref` and an
`expected_revision`. This is what it reads instead.

`can_attest` is computed here rather than in the client precisely because the
client would have to re-derive the route's own precondition — an attestation
requires an edit, so the revision must differ from the analysis output. Deriving
it twice is how a button and the rule it represents drift apart.
RelatedRef.title: RelatedRef

RunGraph.description:
The run's graph, and where execution has reached in it.

``current`` and ``visited`` are what the canvas animates. They are the
platform's, not Studio's: a picture Studio derived from the trace would be a
second source that can disagree with the run it claims to describe.
RunGraph.title: RunGraph

RunUsage.description: Token usage, as the platform reports it for one run.
RunUsage.title: RunUsage

SaveDraftRequest.description: The buffer, and the revision the author believed they were editing.
SaveDraftRequest.title: SaveDraftRequest

SaveDraftResponse.description: The revision recomputed from the bytes that were actually written.
SaveDraftResponse.title: SaveDraftResponse

StageView.description:
One governance stage's verdict.

``ResponseModel`` because ``detail`` is always sent — ``{}`` when a stage
has nothing to add — and the contract said it might be absent. Found by the
spec-driven half of ``test_response_contract``, not by the survey that
produced this change: that survey read ``kneo_studio/schemas/``, and a
response model declared next to its router was outside the net it cast.
StageView.title: StageView

StandingAttestation.description:
Testimony that still stands, and the bytes it was given about.

Both halves, because `(analysis, gap, revision)` is the event's identity and a
withdrawal has to name it. Reporting the gap without the revision is what left
the client deriving the revision from the file — the mistake that produced three
fail-open variants across two external rounds.
StandingAttestation.title: StandingAttestation

StopResult.description:
What asking the platform to stop a run actually did.

**Three outcomes, never collapsed into "it worked"** (0.7.0 S10, review
round 3). The platform answers `200` whether it recorded a cancellation or
had nothing to cancel, so a caller reading the status code alone would
announce a cancellation that never happened.

* ``cancelled`` — the platform returned ``cancelled``. **True of two
  histories** — this request recorded it, or an earlier one did — and the
  status cannot say which, so the sentence claims only what holds for both
  `[touchpoint 2 round 1, F-04]`. This arm was ``already_cancelled`` and read
  every first Stop as a repeat, on the wire and in the audit row.
* ``already_finished`` — it had reached a terminal status. A successful
  **no-op**: not an error, and not silence.
* ``requested`` — a live status came back. The installed producer never
  returns one from a cancel; this is the fallback for one that might.

`message` is the sentence to show. It is server-side because the three
readings turn on the platform's semantics — cooperative cancellation, and no
promise that completed effects are reversed — and a client re-deriving them
would be re-deriving a contract it does not own.
StopResult.title: StopResult

StudioTestRun.title: StudioTestRun

Suggestion.description:
Never a verdict. The policy-report stage's own ``StageView`` is the
authoritative answer, and the SPA must render the two distinctly.
Suggestion.title: Suggestion

TestRunCreateRequest.description:
`{artifact_id, input}` and nothing else.

Closed to extra fields on purpose: alias, generation, profile, environment, the
spec, overlays, overrides, `async_mode`, `session_id` and the idempotency key are
all derived server-side from the artifact and never accepted from the caller. A
body that names one of them is a `422`, not a silently ignored field — the latter
is how a client comes to believe it chose the environment.
TestRunCreateRequest.title: TestRunCreateRequest

TraceWindow.description:
One page of a trace, with everything needed to describe it honestly.

A `ResponseModel`, so every field is **present and nullable** rather than
optional: "the key was missing" and "the platform said null" are not
different answers, and a panel branching on the difference is writing a
branch against nothing.
TraceWindow.title: TraceWindow

get.description: The registry backing the source picker.

The caller, and the projects they may open.

Deliberately **not** behind :func:`authorize`: that helper is
project-scoped, and this route is what the SPA calls to discover which
projects exist for it. Under ``auth_mode = none`` the caller is the
bootstrapped local owner — a real principal owning real rows, not a bypass
(ADR-008/012), which is what keeps 0.2.0's login modes a migration rather
than a rewrite.

401.description: `unauthenticated` — no session, or one that no longer resolves, under a login mode (`static` or `oidc`). Never under `auth_mode = none`.

503.description: The caller's principal is not active in this store — the store is not the one this process bootstrapped. No code of its own (`http_503`).

get.description: The caller's projects. Membership *is* the filter — never a directory.

schema.title: Response List Projects Api Projects Get

401.description: `unauthenticated` — no session, or one that no longer resolves, under a login mode (`static` or `oidc`). Never under `auth_mode = none`.

503.description: Under `auth_mode = none`, the local owner is no longer active (an adopted instance started under `none` again). No code of its own (`http_503`).

post.description:
Create a **managed** project; the creator becomes its owner.

Requires an authenticated caller and answers **401** without one. Not
behind `authorize`, for the same reason as `GET /api/projects`: that helper
is project-scoped and there is no project yet. Unscoped is not
unauthenticated — the bar is *any authenticated principal*
(`bff_routers`), which under `auth_mode = none` is the bootstrapped local
owner.

The request carries only a name: the server allocates
`<workspace_base>/<project-id>`, and a root that equals, contains or sits
inside another project's is refused (`store.projects.create_managed`).
Attaching an existing tree stays an operator-only host command.

422.description: Refused. `request_invalid` when the body or a parameter did not match the endpoint's schema, or a field it admits is one the route refuses, with `details.errors` carrying a per-field list (offending input removed); an operation may also refuse with its own code and no `details`.

get.description:
One project, if the caller is a member of it.

``authorize`` answers **404** when they are not, which is the point: a 403
would confirm the id exists to someone with no business knowing.

422.description: Refused. `request_invalid` when the body or a parameter did not match the endpoint's schema, or a field it admits is one the route refuses, with `details.errors` carrying a per-field list (offending input removed); an operation may also refuse with its own code and no `details`.

get.description:
Candidate analyses for these bytes.

Deliberately a **list**: the same output can carry several analyses, so
"the analysis for these bytes" is not a function (round 21, F-01).
Superseded associations are excluded — inheritance follows only the active
successor (round 22, F-02).

schema.title: Response List Candidates Api Projects  Project Id  Analyses Get

422.description: Refused. `request_invalid` when the body or a parameter did not match the endpoint's schema, or a field it admits is one the route refuses, with `details.errors` carrying a per-field list (offending input removed); an operation may also refuse with its own code and no `details`.

get.description: The exact analysis — titles, details, severities and suggestions.

422.description: Refused. `request_invalid` when the body or a parameter did not match the endpoint's schema, or a field it admits is one the route refuses, with `details.errors` carrying a per-field list (offending input removed); an operation may also refuse with its own code and no `details`.

post.description:
Attest that an edit addressed a blocking card, or withdraw that. **Owner.**

The transition that makes the authoring loop terminate. An imported draft's
analysis is keyed to its content, so editing it leaves the new bytes with no
matching analysis — `unknown`, which does not export — and the one escape,
`assert_not_applicable`, is deliberately refused for a draft that ever carried an
analysis. This is the audited, per-card way through.

**Every precondition here is load-bearing, and one of them is the whole design:**

* the analysis must be **related to the ref** in `manifest_analysis`. One analysis
  can relate to several refs and one ref to several analyses, so neither side may
  be inferred from the other;
* `expected_revision` is compare-and-set against the bytes on disk, so an
  attestation cannot be written about a file that moved under the author;
* an `attest` whose revision equals the analysis's own `output_sha256` is
  **refused**. Without that, an owner could attest against the *unchanged
  imported bytes* for every blocking id and export them — the whole-draft result
  one card at a time.

Answers the effective state and the **recomputed** outstanding set, so an author
learns what remains in one round trip rather than deriving it from a stale list.

422.description: Refused. `request_invalid` when the body or a parameter did not match the endpoint's schema, or a field it admits is one the route refuses, with `details.errors` carrying a per-field list (offending input removed); an operation may also refuse with its own code and no `details`.

get.description:
Every live artifact in the project, newest first.

**Nothing could enumerate them.** An artifact was reachable only by the
navigation that created it, and that navigation lived in transient React
state — so a reload, a new tab or a restart lost the only route to it, on a
product whose pitch is a durable governed unit. Drafts have had a list route
since the first cut; artifacts never got one (external review, F-05).

Soft-deleted artifacts are excluded: `deleted_at` is the tombstone the
export route answers `410` for, and a picker offering them would lead the
reader somewhere that refuses by design.

Same projection as the single read, so a list entry and the page it opens
cannot disagree about the artifact they describe.

schema.title: Response List Artifacts Api Projects  Project Id  Artifacts Get

422.description: Refused. `request_invalid` when the body or a parameter did not match the endpoint's schema, or a field it admits is one the route refuses, with `details.errors` carrying a per-field list (offending input removed); an operation may also refuse with its own code and no `details`.

post.description: Create an artifact from authored inputs and freeze what it inherits.

422.description: Refused. `request_invalid` when the body or a parameter did not match the endpoint's schema, or a field it admits is one the route refuses, with `details.errors` carrying a per-field list (offending input removed); an operation may also refuse with its own code and no `details`.

delete.description:
Soft-delete an artifact and release the snapshot it held. **Editor.**

**The recovery path the save-any-text decision needs.** Once any buffer can be
saved and explicitly frozen, an unwanted creation charges quota with no
user-visible way back — and snapshot GC has nothing to collect for an ordinary
artifact, because nothing ever drops a reference. `store.artifacts.soft_delete`
shipped in 0.1.0 with no caller and was exempted in the declared-but-unwired gate
as *"no delete route yet"*; this is that caller.

**Soft**, not a row deletion: an artifact is a provenance record, and export
refusals, acknowledgements and attestations all point at it. `deleted_at` is what
export reads to answer `410`.

Authorized as `CREATE_ARTIFACT` — the same capability that made the thing.
Deleting your own mistake must not need more authority than making it, and a
separate action would be a role boundary nobody asked for.

One transaction: the tombstone and the reference drop cannot part company, or a
snapshot stays charged forever with nothing pointing at it. The **collection** runs
after the commit, deliberately — it deletes a directory, and filesystem effects do
not belong inside a database transaction.

422.description: Refused. `request_invalid` when the body or a parameter did not match the endpoint's schema, or a field it admits is one the route refuses, with `details.errors` carrying a per-field list (offending input removed); an operation may also refuse with its own code and no `details`.

get.description:
One artifact, as the SPA needs it after a reload.

Creation returned this projection and nothing could fetch it again, so a
page addressed by `artifact_id` — the editor, hand-off — had no way to
learn its own base draft or its analysis state without the navigation that
created it. A refresh emptied the page.

`_reload` is the same projection the acknowledgement response returns, so
the two cannot drift into disagreeing about the artifact they describe.

422.description: Refused. `request_invalid` when the body or a parameter did not match the endpoint's schema, or a field it admits is one the route refuses, with `details.errors` carrying a per-field list (offending input removed); an operation may also refuse with its own code and no `details`.

post.description:
Acknowledge a ``manual`` gap frozen by one of this artifact's analyses.

Round 18 promised export refuses an unacknowledged ``manual`` gap and gave
that gate **no record, route, authorization rule or SPA action** (round 19,
F-03). Editor-only, audited, and idempotent on the full triple — the
``analysis_id`` is part of the key because two inherited analyses may reuse
a local ``gap_id`` (round 20, F-01).

422.description: Refused. `request_invalid` when the body or a parameter did not match the endpoint's schema, or a field it admits is one the route refuses, with `details.errors` carrying a per-field list (offending input removed); an operation may also refuse with its own code and no `details`.

get.description:
Readiness, then a **fresh** govern gate over the exact export body.

post.description:
Carry a draft's analyses to a path holding the same bytes.

**This is what makes a rename survivable.** An analysis relates to a *ref*, and both
the resolution route and artifact creation require the relation to be on the
**current** ref — so after a bare `git mv` the transition simply stops, fail-closed,
with an artifact that cannot be created and gaps that cannot be resolved.

**It moves no file and reads only the target**, so an external `git mv` stays an
ordinary event and no filesystem effect sits inside the transaction.

Copy, not move: the old ref keeps its relations, so `assert_not_applicable` stays
refused there and a reappearing file cannot be laundered into a clean one.

Refusals are the specification's, and each names which side failed —
`reassociation_source_not_found`, `reassociation_source_revision_unknown`,
`draft_stale` with the offending ref, `reassociation_target_conflict`,
`exposure_stale`, and `404 draft_not_found` for anything about the target that
cannot be read. A retry after a lost response is idempotent while the preconditions
still hold; an intervening content or exposure change is not a retry of the same
state and gets the matching stale refusal.

Save a draft. **Any text saves** — validity is not this route's business.

A draft is a *file* (ADR-009). Refusing to persist invalid YAML would lose an
author's work mid-thought and push them to edit outside Studio, which is the
opposite of what the loop is for. Validity is enforced by **preview, the govern
loop and the export gate** — not here, and not at artifact creation, which
resolves an alias and hashes a snapshot without parsing it.

**`expected_revision` is a compare-and-set**, and a mismatch is
`409 draft_stale` carrying `{path, expected_revision, revision}` — the body the
error table already defines for that code. The comparison and the write happen
under one project lock, so a concurrent save cannot land between them.

**Atomic per draft, and not across drafts.** The store writes a temporary file
and renames it, so a concurrent reader sees old or new bytes and never a partial
file. A multi-file save is N independent calls and the client owns the
sequencing: one transaction spanning arbitrary files is a lock-ordering hazard
for no gain.

Writing bytes does **not** create, supersede or invalidate an analysis —
analysis follows content by hash, and what an edited revision needs is the
remediation protocol's attestation.

post.description:
Ask the platform to stop this run.

**Editor-only**, like starting one: it changes what is executing and what it
costs. The only write in the debug loop — `resume` and `replay` are deferred
with their reason in ADR-007's amendment.

**The server's semantics are preserved exactly as they are.** Cancellation
is *cooperative*: the platform records the request and the run stops when it
next reaches a point where it can. So the wording is "requested", and it
never promises that completed effects are reversed — a tool call that
already ran, already ran.

**A terminal run is a successful no-op, not an error and not silence**
(review round 3). The platform answers `200` with the run's *current*
status, and this route reports that returned outcome rather than announcing
a cancellation because HTTP said 200. Three different things that a naive
read would collapse into one:

* the run was still going and cancellation is now requested;
* the run had already finished, and nothing needed cancelling;
* the run was already `cancelled`, which keeps the cooperative wording
  because that is what it means.

**The returned status wins over what the caller thought.** The server's
compare-and-set can hand back a terminal result a concurrent worker won, so
a UI that had rendered "running" a moment ago must consume the answer rather
than its own stale belief.
